purpose: Research-only snapshots for designing one consolidated, demand-matched web-presentation capability. These folders are not registered as project runtime skills and their scripts must not be executed implicitly.
selection_policy: The source contains one or more real SKILL.md files.
The source contributes a distinct presentation-generation, template-selection, pedagogy, or verification capability.
GitHub stars are a popularity signal, not a substitute for relevance, license, maintainability, and project fit.
Only sources whose repository license permits retention are stored in this project.
Large presentation engines without an Agent Skill are benchmarks, not vendored skills.

selected_sources.contribution: Browser-native HTML deck workflow, fixed-stage rendering, visual preview selection, 12 safe presets, and a 34-template bold design pack with compact selection metadata.
Structured intake, scenario routing, semantic inspiration ranking, brand systems, durable project state, and two-signal verification.
Reveal.js structure, horizontal and vertical slide organization, chart layout rules, overflow checks, and screenshot-based visual review.
Source-asset inventory, template-as-source-of-truth, editable output discipline, stale-placeholder detection, and visual quality gates.
Academic presentation pedagogy, five visual themes, a broad layout-pattern pool, formula and diagram affordances, and scored QA.

reviewed_not_vendored.reason: The pptx skill's license explicitly prohibits retaining copies outside Anthropic services and creating derivatives.
Strong scientific-slide specialization, but the very large catalog overlaps the smaller selected academic sources; retain the link as a future benchmark rather than vendoring the catalog.
The repository declares MIT while SKILL.md declares a proprietary license and points to a missing LICENSE.txt; do not retain until provenance is clarified.
Useful presentation engine and HTML-template benchmark, but not an Agent Skill and too large to vendor as a reference skill.
High-quality developer presentation engine, but not a reusable Agent Skill; treat as an implementation benchmark.
Framework rather than Agent Skill; the selected revealjs-skill already packages the relevant workflow.
Markdown presentation engine rather than an Agent Skill; useful only if Markdown-first authoring becomes a product requirement.
